correctness.rationale: In the radical-square-zero height-two incidence algebra, the only commutator condition on edge (u,v) is (d_u-d_v)y_e-(h_u-h_v)x_e=0. For vertex colors (d_u,h_u) in F_q^2 it gives q^2 edge choices on equal colors and q otherwise. Summing yields q^(-m-2v) sum_{colors} prod_e [1+(q-1)1_equal], hence the q^2-state Fortuin--Kasteleyn expansion. Writing q^(-m) sum_F (q-1)^|F|q^(-2r(F)) makes cycle-rank positivity and equality iff forest exact. For fixed G the leading term maximizes |F|-2r(F), and Edmonds matroid-union formula gives s_2(G)=m-max_F(|F|-2r(F)). Independently enumerated edge subsets: K_(3,4) has (s2,nu)=(12,2) and K_(4,4) has (14,1). This does not extend to posets with three-element chains, and q→∞ fixes G.
residual_risks: Height-two and no longer-chain extension; fixed-graph asymptotic; no field-uniform growing-size bound
